stories.title: Georgia's first Black agriculture commissioner-elect faces a backlash
stories.dek: Democrat Katherine Juhan-Arnold won 53% to 46%. Since then a bakery owner's son posted a racist remark and a farmer petitioned lawmakers to probe her credentials, Capital B reports.

stories.title: Rejected ballots leave Tougaloo and Jackson State students shut out
stories.dek: Hundreds of provisional ballots from the two HBCUs went uncounted, many over county mix-ups on Tougaloo's two-county campus. Hinds County rejected over half of its 2,426, Capital B reports.

stories.title: Black-run food bank feeds thousands as federal cuts hit Prince George's
stories.dek: The StoreHouse says it serves about 6,000 families a month. A local pastor ties rising need to federal job losses, citing Capital Area Food Bank data on county hunger, The Washington Informer reports.

stories.title: Jrue and Lauren Holiday's $5.3M fund sparks $3M more for Black founders
stories.dek: Black-owned businesses and Black-led nonprofits backed by the couple's social impact fund have since raised over $3 million in follow-on funding, per the fund, AfroTech reports.

stories.title: Brian Rikuda, a past BET reality show winner, will head the network
stories.dek: Rikuda won BET's The Ultimate Hustler in 2005 and rejoined BET in 2022. He will report to OWN president Tina Perry under Skydance's cable restructuring, Black Enterprise reports, citing Deadline.

stories.title: Vermont nursing home to pay $450K over racist abuse of Black workers
stories.dek: Elderwood at Burlington settled an EEOC suit for six Black nurses and aides who faced slurs and assaults from residents. The companies deny the claims and admit no liability, TheGrio reports.

stories.alt: Giant striped ESSENCE letters on the ESSENCE Stage at the 30th ESSENCE Festival of Culture in New Orleans
stories.title: ESSENCE Fest will leave New Orleans in 2027 after 33 years
stories.dek: Owner Sundial Media Group says talks on a multiyear deal failed. Mayor Helena Moreno cited unpaid local vendors and says a Black-led festival will take its place, That Grape Juice reports.

stories.alt: Ta-Nehisi Coates in a black turtleneck against a terracotta wall
stories.title: Ta-Nehisi Coates unveils Maceo-Lyn Productions with two partners
stories.dek: Coates, director Kamilah Forbes and producer Kenyatta Matthews announced the film, TV and theater company, whose slate includes a Basquiat musical with music by John Legend, Black Enterprise reports.

stories.title: Obama urges incoming House Democrats to push further on health care
stories.dek: At a Nov. 18 meeting, Obama said restoring expired ACA subsidies alone is not enough. Black HealthCare.gov sign-ups fell from about 2.7 million to 1.2 million, per figures Word In Black cites.

stories.title: Federal cuts halt Alzheimer's research focused on Black Americans
stories.dek: NIH ended a four-year Pittsburgh study in the Hill and Homewood near its final year, and an Emory study on racism's effects needs $2.3 million to finish, TheGrio reports.

stories.alt: Aaron Douglas's 1931 Harriet Tubman painting: blue-green silhouettes, a central figure raising arms with broken chains
stories.vidTitle: Kasi Lemmons on Aaron Douglas' Harriet Tubman
stories.title: Aaron Douglas's Harriet Tubman painting sells for $14.4M at Sotheby's
stories.dek: Bennett College sold the 1931 work, far above a $2.5M-$3.5M estimate, to fund a women's health initiative. Some students and alumni opposed the sale, Black Enterprise reports.

stories.title: Playbill apologizes for a George Floyd musical casting notice
stories.dek: Playbill pulled the job-board listing and says it is reviewing approvals after criticism, including from Viola Davis. Producer Busted Broadway calls the show satire, Black Enterprise reports.

stories.title: Eatonville data center drops its promise of free home Wi-Fi
stories.dek: HostDime's CEO says free home Wi-Fi for the historic Black town is no longer sustainable; it now offers public Wi-Fi, and promised scholarships are unclear, Capital B reports.

stories.title: Raleigh renter evicted after an AI chatbot okayed a late-rent extension
stories.dek: Laura Mack got an email extension on nearly $4,000 in back rent from the complex's chatbot, then an eviction notice. The landlord says the bot acted without its knowledge, AfroTech reports, citing WRAL.

stories.alt: Janelle James smiling beside the Grand Theft Auto VI logo
stories.credit: Janelle James: ESSENCE · GTA VI logo: Rockstar Games
stories.title: GTA VI is out, with Black stars voicing roles and hosting its radio
stories.dek: Janelle James hosts and co-wrote an in-game radio show, TLC runs an R&B station and Burna Boy hosts an Afrobeats one in the Nov. 19 release, TheGrio reports.

stories.alt: D'Angelo in a black hat and scarf, beside the GTA VI Radio logo
stories.credit: D'Angelo: Gregory Harris for GQ · GTA VI Radio logo: Rockstar Games
stories.title: An unreleased D'Angelo song plays on GTA VI's radio
stories.dek: His estate says Kamikazi, which he approved in 2024, airs on the game's Worldwide FM station and will be released outside the game, with a vinyl edition planned, TheGrio reports.

stories.alt: Nneka Ogwumike #30 of the Los Angeles Sparks celebrates after the game against the New York Liberty at Crypto.com Arena on June 21, 2026, in Los Angeles
stories.title: Kwanza Jones and José Feliciano near a record $750M Sparks purchase
stories.dek: Citing Sportico, TheGrio reports the couple is close to buying the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks from Mark Walter. The deal is not final; it would top the $300 million paid for the Sun.

stories.title: Shedeur Sanders covers shoppers' groceries in Cleveland before Thanksgiving
stories.dek: The Browns quarterback paid for groceries at Dave's Market on Nov. 24 and waved more families to the registers so he could help them too, TheGrio reports, citing News 5 Cleveland.

stories.title: Teyana Taylor graduates from culinary school
stories.dek: The Golden Globe winner finished at the Auguste Escoffier School of Culinary Arts on Nov. 15 and called the experience therapeutic, TheGrio reports.

stories.title: The Melanie Dolls land on H-E-B shelves in Houston
stories.dek: Founder Datreese Thomas, 27, says H-E-B told her it's the retailer's first direct-delivery vendor selling Black dolls. She is seeking $5 million to expand, AfroTech reports.

stories.title: Student homelessness hits a record, with Black students a quarter of the total
stories.dek: National Center for Homeless Education data show 1.55 million homeless students in 2024-25, up 13.1% in two years; 25.4% are Black. Some states identified fewer students after aid ended, AfroTech reports.

stories.title: Morehouse orders an outside review of how it handles sexual misconduct
stories.dek: After campus police arrested a student on a rape allegation Nov. 13, President F. DuBois Bowman announced a Title IX review and a task force on student safety, Capital B Atlanta reports.

stories.title: Tennessee State builds the only HBCU mining engineering program
stories.dek: TSU's minor, funded by an $800,000 Energy Department grant, has about 15 students and could become a major, US Black Engineer reports.

stories.title: Ohio State's James L. Moore III elected to two national academies
stories.dek: The former NSF engineering program director joined the National Academy of Education and the Academy of Public Administration, US Black Engineer reports.

stories.title: Kid Cudi will release a dance album as RAGER on Dec. 10
stories.dek: Cudi announced Visions in the Night on social media, with artwork due Nov. 30 and the tracklist Dec. 7. Collaborators and track count are not yet known, That Grape Juice reports.

stories.title: Pandora launches AGENDA, an R&B station centering queer artists
stories.dek: Built by SiriusXM/Pandora R&B programming head Akim Bryant, the station launched Nov. 25 with music and commentary from artists including Kehlani, Syd and Durand Bernarr, GAYE Magazine reports.

stories.title: Black family wealth fell 25% as U.S. wealth rose, Fed survey shows
stories.dek: Median Black family net worth dropped from $49,100 to $36,800 between 2022 and 2025, the only group to fall, per the Federal Reserve survey, The Community Voice reports.

stories.title: Greenwood Bank closes all accounts and points members to DreamFi
stories.dek: Cards and transfers stopped after Nov. 19. Deposits stay at Coastal Community Bank until members move them or get a check; Ben Crump's DreamFi is the new partner, AfroTech reports.

stories.alt: A still from 14th: two women talk across a desk in a wood-paneled office beside an American flag
stories.title: Ava DuVernay's 14th is in select theaters now and streams on Netflix Dec. 4
stories.dek: Her follow-up to 13th traces more than 150 years of the 14th Amendment through 50-plus interviews. It opened in select theaters Nov. 27 after closing the New York Film Festival.

stories.alt: Keke Palmer smiles and holds up a purple Apple Podcasts icon against a pink-to-purple background
stories.title: Keke Palmer's podcast is Apple's 2026 Show of the Year
stories.dek: Apple Podcasts named Baby, This Is Keke Palmer, her Wondery interview show, its 2026 Show of the Year, citing its mix of celebrity talk and life topics. Guests have included Oprah Winfrey.

stories.title: Melanin Beauty Awards honor Chaka Khan, Jackie Aina and Shontay Lundy
stories.dek: MadameNoire and HelloBeautiful held their first in-person edition Nov. 18 in New York. Black Girl Sunscreen's Lundy was named beauty founder of the year, MadameNoire reports of its own event.

stories.title: Consumer Reports finds trace lead in lipsticks, including a Black-owned brand
stories.dek: All 24 lipsticks tested passed the FDA draft limit of 10 ppm, but Mented Cosmetics' semi-matte averaged 1.64 ppm, above Washington state's 1.0 ppm cap, Word In Black reports.

stories.alt: A scene from The Airport: a smiling pilot in uniform in the cockpit
stories.title: KevOnStage's improv sitcom The Airport lands on Tubi
stories.dek: All 10 episodes premiered Nov. 19. Kevin Fredricks leads a cast of more than 45 comedians and creators, including Tabitha Brown, Tony Baker and Spice Adams, That Grape Juice reports.

stories.title: Druski's megachurch comedy Collect & Praise hits Netflix Dec. 1
stories.dek: The semi-scripted series, built from his viral pastor sketch, casts Druski as a money-hungry megachurch pastor and Mike Epps as his deacon. The trailer arrived Nov. 18, Complex reports.

stories.title: Thanksgiving food giveaways reach metro Atlanta during Feast Week
stories.dek: The Arena at Southlake set food-box giveaways Nov. 23 in downtown Atlanta and Nov. 24 in Morrow, aiming to serve 750-plus residents downtown, before a D-Nice residency, Black Enterprise reports.

stories.title: A South Memphis pastor's organic farm grows into a food hub
stories.dek: The Rev. Marlon Foster's Green Leaf Learning Farm, the area's only USDA-certified organic farm, anchors cooking classes, a cafe and an Organic Market that opened Oct. 30, Capital B reports.

stories.title: Meet Malik Brown, the Black gay strategist behind Bottoms' win
stories.dek: Brown was deputy campaign manager for operations on Keisha Lance Bottoms' run for Georgia governor and earlier served as Atlanta's first director of LGBTQ affairs, GAYE Magazine reports.

stories.title: Former PragerU host Xaviaer DuRousseau sues, alleging racism and anti-gay abuse
stories.dek: LGBTQ Nation reports the Black gay conservative influencer filed in California Superior Court, claiming discrimination, retaliation and wrongful termination. PragerU denies the allegations.

stories.title: Tevon Blair's Vote HBCU keeps student organizing going after the vote
stories.dek: The Dillard alum leads Xceleader's nonpartisan Vote HBCU, which runs voter education and campus fellows. GAYE Magazine profiles his mentoring of students, including a Black queer Hampton fellow.

stories.alt: A scene from P-Valley in a dressing room lit by a glowing mirror frame
stories.title: Toni Bryce on P-Valley's final season and Black trans visibility
stories.dek: Bryce, a Black trans performer, plays house mother Nineveh. The Starz drama's nine-episode final season starts Dec. 4 with two episodes, GAYE Magazine reports.

stories.title: Lena Waithe's Around the Table readings spotlight Black masc writers
stories.dek: Waithe's new monthly Los Angeles series stages original scripts as live readings. GAYE Magazine profiles her chief of staff, Brooklynn Fields, whose co-written script the LET OUT was read Nov. 19.

regional.title: D.C. sues a developer over 36 vacant Ward 8 apartments
regional.dek: AG Brian Schwalb says the owner got city-backed loans to rehab the buildings and keep 18 units affordable but fixed none; 94 code violations remain, The Washington Informer reports.

regional.title: Black running clubs turn out for the Philadelphia Marathon
regional.dek: Black Girls Run and Black Men Run members are racing and running support stations at the 33rd marathon weekend, which expects nearly 40,000 runners, The Philadelphia Tribune reports.

regional.title: Birmingham school board extends Superintendent Mark Sullivan to 2030
regional.dek: The two-year extension follows a meets-expectations rating of 3.1 out of 4 and the district's record-high state report card score of 79, The Birmingham Times reports.

regional.title: Norman Mitchell, five-term Mecklenburg commissioner, dies at 79
regional.dek: Mitchell represented District 2 from 1998 to 2008, pushed health and veteran services and west Charlotte development, and later served as a state ABC commissioner, The Charlotte Post reports.

regional.title: Gary weighs a U.S. Steel deal tied to a $3 billion mill investment
regional.dek: The proposal would erase $99 million in city debt and fund housing and public safety. It needs City Council approval, and one council leader wants an outside consultant first, Capital B Gary reports.

regional.title: SLU custodians face pay and benefit cuts as cleaning work is outsourced
regional.dek: Saint Louis University is laying off 67 custodians and moving the work to HES. SEIU Local 1 says wages drop $1 to $1.50 an hour; SLU cites turnover, The St. Louis American reports.

regional.title: Dallas builder Royce Colley opens doors for aspiring Black builders
regional.dek: Dallas Weekly's Best of Black Dallas profile notes Black owners were 1.7% of U.S. construction firms with employees in 2022, per Brookings and Census data cited in the piece.

regional.title: Texas Southern fires football coach Cris Dishman after a 3-8 season
regional.dek: Dishman went 14-17 in three seasons at the SWAC school and is owed $319,000 for his last contract year. TSU plans a national search, the Houston Defender reports.

regional.title: Brotherhood Crusade hands out Thanksgiving meals in the rain in South L.A.
regional.dek: The group's drive-through Grab and Go on Nov. 19 at Algin Sutton Recreation Center gave out turkeys and meal items, with gift cards for the first 500 cars, the Los Angeles Sentinel reports.

regional.title: Seattle Black College Expo offers a record $10 million in scholarships
regional.dek: More than 40 HBCUs and other schools joined the ninth expo Nov. 14 at Highline College, and some students got on-the-spot admission, The Seattle Medium reports. Washington has no HBCUs.

weekly.title: Georgia's first Black agriculture commissioner-elect faces a backlash
weekly.dek: Democrat Katherine Juhan-Arnold won 53% to 46%. Since then a bakery owner's son posted a racist remark and a farmer petitioned lawmakers to probe her credentials, Capital B reports.

weekly.dek: Cards and transfers stopped after Nov. 19. Deposits stay at Coastal Community Bank until members move them or get a check; Ben Crump's DreamFi is the new partner, AfroTech reports.

monthly.title: Jaelynn Scott wins a Washington House seat, a first for Black trans women
monthly.dek: Scott took about 87% of the vote in Seattle's 37th District. Gaye Magazine reports she is the first openly Black transgender woman elected to a state legislature.

monthly.title: Charleston opens a memorial to the Emanuel Nine at Mother Emanuel
monthly.dek: The 6,000-square-foot stone memorial beside the church opens Nov. 14 with a 9 a.m. public ceremony. TheGrio reports it cost $20 million, funded mostly by donations.

monthly.title: Valkyries-Dream Finals draws the WNBA's biggest audience since 1999
monthly.dek: The seven-game series against the Atlanta Dream averaged 1.88 million viewers, up 30% from 2025, the league says. Game 7 drew 3.3 million, a record for a WNBA playoff game.
